# Dynamic Fan-out with Hatchet TypeScript SDK

## Background

Hatchet is a distributed task queue and workflow engine that supports durable execution and dynamic child spawning. In this task, you will use the `@hatchet-dev/typescript-sdk` to implement a parent task that dynamically fans out work to multiple child tasks at runtime, awaits their results, and aggregates them.

The Hatchet client connects to **Hatchet Cloud**. A real `HATCHET_CLIENT_TOKEN` is provided in the environment. **Do NOT mock the Hatchet SDK or any of its behavior** — the task MUST connect to the real Hatchet Cloud control plane, run a real worker, register real tasks, and execute real task runs end-to-end.

## Requirements

* Implement two Hatchet tasks in TypeScript using `@hatchet-dev/typescript-sdk`:
  * A child task named `square-item-${run-id}` that accepts an input `{ n: number }` and returns `{ square: n*n }`.
  * A parent task named `process-batch-${run-id}` that accepts `{ items: number[] }`. For each item in `items`, it must spawn the child task and await its result. The parent must return `{ squares: number[] }` where each entry is the square of the corresponding input item (preserving order).
* Start a Hatchet worker that registers both tasks and connects to Hatchet Cloud using `HATCHET_CLIENT_TOKEN`.
* Trigger the parent task with the concrete input `{ items: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] }` and write the returned output to `/tmp/result.json` as a JSON object with shape `{ "squares": [1, 4, 9, 16, 25] }`.
* The runner must shut down cleanly after writing the result so the container exits.

## Implementation Hints

* Use `@hatchet-dev/typescript-sdk` and run TypeScript directly with `tsx`.
* Read `run-id` from the `ZEALT_RUN_ID` environment variable and append it as a suffix to all Hatchet task names (child + parent) to avoid collisions with other concurrent runs sharing the same Hatchet account.
* Look up the child-spawning pattern in the Hatchet docs (`https://docs.hatchet.run/home/child-spawning`). The TypeScript SDK supports spawning a child by calling `.run(input)` on the child task object from within the parent's `fn`. Use `Promise.all` to fan out and await all children in parallel.
* Hatchet Cloud server URL is the default in the SDK — do **NOT** set `HATCHET_CLIENT_HOST_PORT` or any custom server address.
* The worker must be started in the same process (or a sibling process) so that the parent and child task registrations are picked up before triggering the parent. After the parent's run completes, write the result file and exit.
* Place all code under `/home/user/myproject`. A `package.json` with `@hatchet-dev/typescript-sdk`, `typescript`, and `tsx` must be set up so the project can be run with `npx tsx <entry>.ts` or `npm start`.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Project path: /home/user/myproject
* Output file: /tmp/result.json
* The Hatchet child task name must be `square-item-${run-id}` and the parent task name must be `process-batch-${run-id}`, where `run-id` is read from the `ZEALT_RUN_ID` environment variable.
* The implementation must use the real `@hatchet-dev/typescript-sdk` against Hatchet Cloud. No mocks or stand-ins are allowed.
* The parent task must spawn one child task per input item (dynamic fan-out at runtime, not via a statically declared DAG with named parents).
* After execution, `/tmp/result.json` must be a valid JSON file containing exactly `{"squares": [1, 4, 9, 16, 25]}` (the order must match the order of the input items).

# Hatchet TypeScript SDK
[![npm version](https://badge.fury.io/js/@hatchet-dev%2Ftypescript-sdk.svg)](https://badge.fury.io/js/@hatchet-dev%2Ftypescript-sdk) [![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-hatchet.run-blue)](https://docs.hatchet.run) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-purple.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)
This is the official TypeScript SDK for [Hatchet](https://hatchet.run), a distributed, fault-tolerant task queue. The SDK provides a type-safe way to integrate Hatchet's task scheduling and workflow orchestration capabilities into your TypeScript/JavaScript applications. ## Installation Install the SDK using npm: ```bash npm install @hatchet-dev/typescript-sdk ``` Using yarn: ```bash yarn add @hatchet-dev/typescript-sdk ``` Using pnpm: ```bash pnpm add @hatchet-dev/typescript-sdk ``` ## Quick Start For examples of how to use the Hatchet TypeScript SDK, including worker setup and task execution, please see our [official documentation](https://docs.hatchet.run/home/setup). ## Features - 📝 **Type Safety**: Full TypeScript support with type inference for workflow inputs and outputs - 🔄 **Workflow Orchestration**: Define complex workflows with dependencies and parallel execution - 🔁 **Automatic Retries**: Configure retry policies for handling transient failures - 📊 **Observability**: Track workflow progress and monitor execution metrics - ⏰ **Scheduling**: Schedule workflows to run at specific times or on a recurring basis - 🔄 **Event-Driven**: Trigger workflows based on events in your system ## Documentation For detailed documentation, examples, and best practices, visit: - [Hatchet Documentation](https://docs.hatchet.run) - [Examples](https://github.com/hatchet-dev/hatchet/tree/main/sdks/typescript/src/v1/examples) ## Development We use `pnpm` as our package manager. To get started with development: 1. Install dependencies: ```bash pnpm install ``` 2. Build the SDK: ```bash pnpm build ``` 3. Run unit tests: ```bash pnpm test:unit ``` 4. Run e2e tests (requires a running Hatchet engine): ```bash # Run all e2e tests pnpm test:e2e # Run a specific e2e test file pnpm test:e2e durable.e2e.ts # Run a specific test by name pnpm test:e2e durable.e2e.ts -t "durable replay reset" ``` ## Contributing We welcome contributions! Please check out our [contributing guidelines](https://docs.hatchet.run/contributing) and join our [Discord community](https://hatchet.run/discord) for discussions and support. ## License This SDK is released under the MIT License. See [LICENSE](https://github.com/hatchet-dev/hatchet/blob/main/LICENSE) for details.
